Karthik / team / Clara — quick engineering sizing notes below (keeps to conservative estimates for committed capacity). TL;DR: KV cache dominates for very long contexts and is largely independent of weight quantization; quantization helps model weights but not KV cache unless you also store KV in lower precision which increases risk to numeric stability.

Assumptions and baseline numbers (conservative):
- Model parameter memory (weights): stored quantized on GPU. 8-bit quant -> ~0.5x float16 weight size; 4-bit (groupwise) -> ~0.25x.
- KV cache memory: per token, per layer store for Keys + Values. For an attention layer with d_model ~ 8192 (typical for 33B family), KV per token ~ 2 * d_model * bytes_per_element. If stored in fp16 (2 bytes), KV per token per layer ~ 2 * 8192 * 2 = ~32KB. Multiply by number of layers: 80 layers -> ~2.5MB per token.
- That means 64k context -> ~160GB just for KV cache (64k * 2.5MB ≈ 160GB). 128k -> ~320GB.

Practical implications:
- Weight quantization (4/8-bit) reduces model weight footprint but does NOT reduce KV cache footprint unless we also quantize KV (possible but increases latency and can degrade attention fidelity).
- For long contexts (64k+), KV cache will exceed single 80GB GPU by far. You will need KV sharding across host memory/GPU pool or explicit KV offload to CPU/NVMe, which increases latency.

Recommended configurations (monthly Dedicated commits) — per workload:
1) 7B at 128k context (fine-tuned medical):
   - Model weights small enough to fit on a single 80GB GPU if 4-bit quantized.
   - KV cache estimate: ~128k * (approx 0.3MB/token for smaller d_model) -> ~38GB (smaller models ~12 layers, d_model smaller). BUT for medical fine-tuned 7B with large context optimization we still expect KV in the 20–60GB range.
   - Recommended: 1xA100-80GB (weights + local KV) + 1xA100-80GB as KV-shard / overflow OR a single H100-80GB with CPU-offload path and streaming prefix cache. Consider using Redwood Optimize rules to prefix-cache common sections to reduce effective KV.
2) 33B at 64k context:
   - Weight footprint (8-bit): ~40–60GB depending on optimizer state; with 4-bit can compress further to ~20–30GB.
   - KV cache (~2.5MB/token estimate above): 64k -> ~160GB.
   - Recommended: KV must be sharded across ~3–4x80GB GPUs (model + KV). Typical config: 2 GPUs for model-parallel (weights), 2 GPUs dedicated to KV shards; right-sizing tends to be 4x80GB (A100/H100) for stable latency. If you want single-session p99 < 400ms, avoid full CPU offload — keep KV in GPU memory across the shard set.
3) 70B at 32k context:
   - Weights: even quantized, 70B tends to need multi-GPU model-parallel (2–4 GPUs) for weights alone.
   - KV: 32k * 2.5MB ≈ 80GB (so one 80GB GPU could hold KV but leaves little room for weights).
   - Recommended: 4x80GB cluster (2 GPUs for model slices, 2 for KV) or move to H100 pods for better NVLink bandwidth and lower p99.

Latency tradeoffs and options:
- CPU-offload (NVMe or host RAM) reduces committed GPU count but can add 2–10x latency on p99 depending on access patterns; not recommended for p99-sensitive chat.
- KV quantization: possible to store KV in 8-bit/fp8-ish formats to halve KV size; we can prototype but expect a small accuracy hit. Good candidate for non-safety-critical retrieval augmentation, less so for clinical summarization.
- Streaming/prefix caching: if many requests share prefixes (patient metadata, note headers), prefix caching reduces KV growth dramatically. Redwood Optimize can detect and pin common prefixes to accelerate.

Operational recommendations for the deal:
- Start committed pool: 4xA100-80GB (or 4xH100) reserved for initial PoC across the three models with autoscaling burst to 8 GPUs for peak batch work. Use policy to route heavier inferences to dedicated nodes during business hours.
- Include an explicit KV sizing clause in SOW (we will run a 2-week load test with representative 64k/128k traces to right-size).
- Offer two pricing tiers: (a) conservative committed pool (4x80GB) + burst; (b) proactive multi-pod (8x80GB) if Medyssey wants single-digit p99 with no CPU-offload.

I can prepare an appendix with the per-layer math and a small benchmark plan (we should run a 10-user concurrency test and a 50-concurrent retrieval test). If you want, I can also prototype KV-8bit storage on one model to measure quality delta.

-Marissa
